scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
The 1492 to 1500 imported polygon is unchanged and unverified. It covers parts of central Arizona but is not a verified boundary of every Akimel O’odham community.
Akimel O’odham, Tohono O’odham and Piipaash are not treated as interchangeable. Joint institutions and shared museum teaching structures are explicitly identified.
The community word huhugam and the archaeological term Hohokam have different meanings and temporal scopes. No disappearance or unique cause of settlement change around 1450 is asserted.

The irrigation teaching resource predates the 2004 settlement; its projected construction totals and imminent-settlement language are not presented as current facts. Its protohistoric dates are approximate.

The 1859 legal mechanism is described differently by the community timeline and 2019 testimony; neither mechanism is repeated. The 1879 boundary reductions are not converted into a conquest or fall date.
The community history calls ancestral canals the most advanced in North America; that unbounded superlative is omitted. No unsupported exact canal length or continuous operating history is claimed.

Museum structures have no stated construction date. Mary Sampson’s catalogue creation date is explicit and separate from acquisition. Pee Posh pottery in the heritage collection is not reassigned to Akimel artists.

The 2019 testimony establishes enactment in 2004 and enforceability in 2007 for the water settlement. It is not evidence that every proposed Blackwater land-transfer provision passed or every water need has been met.
Independent historical review and geometry assessment remain pending.
